question: What is another common name for Gallows traction?
explanation: You'll often hear Gallows traction called Bryant's traction in the ward! It's named after the surgeon who first used it to help young children heal. You've got this! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h1)

question: Why is Gallows traction only used for babies under two years old?

options.A: Toddlers over two refuse to lie flat
options.B: The straps are just too small for older kids
options.C: Heavier kids can lift their bodies and ruin the pull
options.D: Older children have bones that are too brittle

explanation: Think about it like a see-saw: if a toddler is too heavy, they'll pull themselves up and lift their bottom right off the bed. That ruins the counter-traction needed for the bone to heal! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h1)

question: How should the weights attached to Gallows traction hang?

options.A: Hanging freely without touching the floor or bed
options.B: Resting gently on the edge of the mattress
options.C: Adjusted by parents every few hours

explanation: Weights need to swing completely free in the air to give the exact pulling force required. If they touch the floor, the weight is off! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h2)

question: How high should an infant's bottom be from the mattress in Gallows traction?

options.A: Lifted just barely so a hand can slide underneath
options.B: Raised at least twelve inches high

explanation: Just a tiny lift is the magic trick! It uses the baby's own upper body weight to create the counter-pulling force. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h2)

question: How do nurses check for pain or nerve issues in a baby who cannot talk yet?

options.B: Ask parents to translate facial expressions
options.C: Check muscle electricity with a monitor
options.D: Look for constant crying and restlessness

explanation: Babies can't tell us where it hurts, so we watch their mood! Inconsolable crying and fussiness are their way of saying something is wrong. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h3)

question: A baby in Gallows traction has cool toes and a capillary refill of 4 seconds. What is your first step?

options.B: Put a warm blanket on their feet

explanation: Cool toes and slow refill mean blood flow isn't reaching the foot properly. That's an urgent call to the doctor to protect the limb! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h3)

question: What is a major hygiene worry for an infant in Gallows traction?

options.A: Urine and stool getting on the traction tapes and skin

explanation: With the baby's hips up in the air and wearing a diaper in a tight spot, leaks happen. Keeping this area clean is a major nursing duty to stop infections! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h4)

question: Why must nurses change bed linens with extra care during Gallows traction?

options.A: To stop the baby from rolling onto their stomach
options.B: To keep the fracture and traction setup perfectly aligned
options.C: To keep the weights from breaking
options.D: To save money on hospital laundry

explanation: Any sudden shake can disturb the healing bone and cause great pain. Smooth, careful movements are key! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a common complication of Gallows traction?
explanation: Traction focuses on the legs, skin, and breathing, but it has zero connection to a child's eyesight. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h5)

question: Why might a baby in Gallows traction have trouble breathing deeply?

options.A: The ropes block fresh air from their face
options.B: The sticky tape gives off lung-irritating fumes
options.C: The heavy weights make the room air too thin
options.D: The elevated legs push up on the tummy and limit lung expansion

explanation: Lifting those legs straight up presses the tummy contents against the diaphragm, which can slightly crowd the lungs. Good catch for nursing assessments! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h5)

question: How can you best support parents whose baby is in Gallows traction?

options.A: Tell them not to touch the child at all
options.B: Explain the setup and involve them in gentle, non-physical comforting
options.C: Ask them to leave the room until it's over
options.D: Teach them how to adjust the heavy weights

explanation: Parents feel helpless seeing their baby in traction. Teaching them how to talk, sing, and stroke the baby keeps that parent-child bond strong! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is a great play activity for an infant in Gallows traction?

options.A: Taking them out for a crawling race
options.B: Placing heavy building blocks on their bed tray
options.C: Encouraging them to kick a small football
options.D: Hanging soft toys where they can easily see them

explanation: Since the baby is flat on their back, colourful mobiles and soft hanging toys keep their mind busy and happy without messing up the traction! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h6)

question: What tells you that an infant is ready to come out of Gallows traction?

options.A: The baby turns two years old
options.B: The ropes are starting to look worn out
options.C: X-rays show the bone has healed well with good callus formation
options.D: The parents ask for the metal frame to be taken down

explanation: We don't guess—we check! Only an X-ray proving the bone is strong enough will greenlight removing the traction. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h7)

question: What is a normal finding right after Gallows traction is removed?

options.A: Complete loss of feeling in both legs
options.B: One leg suddenly growing longer than the other
options.C: Running and walking right away without help
options.D: Stiffness in the hips and knees from lying still

explanation: Keeping those little legs up in the air for weeks makes the joints stiff. Gentle stretching and movement will get them back to normal in no time! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h7)
